key_insight: Non-dimensionalization can determine PINN trainability: free-fall scaling avoids the large buoyancy coefficient that drives gradient imbalance under thermal-diffusive scaling.
engineering_relevance: Choosing physically appropriate scaling before training can improve PINN heat-transfer predictions for buoyancy-driven engineering flows.
method: Compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall scalings under identical training conditions.
Study a differentially heated square cavity at Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10³–10⁵.
Measure loss gradients and test sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting.
evidence_signal: Free-fall scaling achieved mean Nusselt-number errors below 1.1% for Ra ≤ 10⁴, while diffusive scaling produced 157–650% errors and diverged at Ra = 10⁵.
watch_item: Free-fall scaling still missed the transient Nusselt-number overshoot in unsteady convection, despite accurately predicting long-time heat transfer.
paper_title: Inherent Failure Modes of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Buoyancy-Driven Flow: Role of Non-Dimensionalization in Network Training
